thread.title: Homeland Security modifies list of airports for Ebola-related arrival restrictions
thread.title_full: Homeland Security modifies list of airports for Ebola-related arrival restrictions

author: s. a. harvey
title: Homeland Security modifies list of airports for Ebola-related arrival restrictions
text:
The Department of Homeland Security announced on May 26 that it has modified the list of designated U.S. airports receiving flights from travelers who have recently been in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Uganda, or South Sudan, in response to the ongoing Ebola outbreak.
According to a directive from the Secretary of Homeland Security, all such flights are required to arrive at Washington-Dulles International Airport (IAD), where the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention is focusing public health resources. The arrival restrictions apply to flights departing after 11:59 p.m. Eastern Daylight Time on Wednesday, May 20.
The directive defines a person as having recently traveled from one of these countries if they departed from or were present within them within 21 days prior to entry or attempted entry into the United States. Crew members and cargo-only flights are excluded from these measures. The notice also states that changes to the list of designated airports may be published in the Federal Register or posted as an advisory at www.cbp.gov.
Previously, Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport (ATL) and George Bush Intercontinental Airport (IAH) had been added to this list by U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP). The current modification adds another airport effective for flights departing after 11:59 p.m. Eastern Daylight Time on Thursday, May 28, with enhanced public health measures implemented at this location as well.
These arrival restrictions will remain until they are superseded, modified, or revoked through publication in the Federal Register. CBP states that advisories about such modifications will be posted at www.cbp.gov.
